The pool has 43 ICML 2025 main-conference project pages: the 10 existing project entries from entries.json plus 33 new ones I verified. I added arxiv_id to each and gave it a selection_reason that quotes its arXiv comment. entries.json also has 3 researcher-kind entries labeled "ICML 2025 Outstanding Paper" (Raghunathan, Snell, Nagarajan). I left them out because they are researcher homepages, not project pages. I did not need the fallback queries ("Accepted to/at ICML 2025") because the main query already returned 50 results, which was enough.

Six results from the main query were excluded:
- Three were workshop papers: BIMgent 2506.07217, Supernova Event Dataset 2506.12189, and UnivEarth 2504.12110 (ICML 2025 Workshop TerraBytes / ACL 2026 Findings).
- Two linked only to bare GitHub repos: Morse 2506.18251 and LLM-SRBench 2504.10415.
- Q-resafe 2506.20251 had no URL at all.

ELITE 2502.04757 (velpegor.github.io/ELITE/) returned 404 and was dropped.

Three recorded URLs differ from the arXiv text because of redirects:
- weborganizer.allen.ai has an HTTP redirect to allenai.github.io/weborganizer-website/.
- williamium3000.github.io/core-knowledge is a meta-refresh stub pointing to grow-ai-like-a-child.github.io/core-knowledge/.
- research.nvidia.com/labs/dir/ddo/ is a meta-refresh stub pointing to research.nvidia.com/labs/cosmos-lab/ddo/.

Many comments say only "ICML 2025" or "ICML 2025 Spotlight" with no word like "accepted". I counted these as stating acceptance, which is the convention the existing entries already follow. The pool has 56 entries: 22 existing researcher entries from entries.json that fall under part 1, carried over with their fields unchanged, plus 34 new homepages. Each new URL returned 200 text/html to curl -sIL, and its body was checked for the person's name and an expected affiliation or paper keyword. Homepage links came from the people's own GitHub profile blog field, Wikidata P856, Semantic Scholar's homepage field, or search results showing the person's own site, and every one was confirmed by fetching it. notes:
Pool: 86 researcher entries. 76 are new; 10 are existing entries kept unchanged (Qi, Ren, Sutherland, A. Wang, Yaodong Yang, Novotny, Jianyuan Wang, plus Choi, LeCun and Bengio, who are filed in entries.json under other awards but also meet this rule). Each new URL returned 200 text/html on a final curl -sIL pass, and every <title> or page text names the person. Where a URL redirected, I stored the effective URL.

Award sources: official ICLR blog posts, CVPR thecvf pages (2023 and 2024), ACL program pages and ACL portal Test-of-Time announcements. For CVPR 2025 I used the IEEE TCPAMI list, because I could not reach the official thecvf 2025 awards page. That list files Navigation World Models under 2024, and I recorded it as CVPR 2025. I counted CVPR's Longuet-Higgins Prize as its Test of Time award, and the ICLR Test of Time runner-ups as well.

Coverage gaps (these need a decision):
(1) I did not cover ACL Outstanding Papers: 38 in 2023, 35 in 2024 and 26 in 2025, about 200 more authors. Only Best Paper and Test of Time are covered for ACL. ICLR Outstanding and Honorable Mention are fully enumerated.
(2) Found but dropped because this machine cannot connect to the host (curl and WebFetch both fail with connection refused or reset): Ben Poole (cs.stanford.edu/~poole), Ben Mildenhall (bmild.com), Zeyuan Allen-Zhu (zeyuan.allen-zhu.com), Hinrich Schütze (cis.lmu.de/schuetze), Christopher Manning (nlp.stanford.edu/~manning), Sanmi Koyejo (cs.stanford.edu/~sanmi). They can be re-verified from another network.
(3) Excluded after checking: Donggyun Kim (Google Site redirects to a login page), Vincent Sitzmann (vsitzmann.github.io returns a GitHub Pages 404), Max Welling (staff page 404), Thang Luong (thangluong.com is a 'Coming Soon' page), Ruoxi Jia (ruoxijia.info returns an empty body), Ferhan Ture (UMIACS 404), Ying Wei (wei-ying.net is a lab site), Boxin Shi and Florian Bernard (personal domains redirect to lab sites), Mario Fritz and Jianfeng Gao (institutional profiles only).
(4) No personal homepage found through the person's own links (DBLP, OpenReview and S2 were rate-limited or blocked): Yuanzhi Li, Anton Bakhtin, Whittington, Mallat, Ido Amos, Ankit Gupta (IBM), Saremi, Darcet, Bojanowski, Yichen Wu, Suyu Ge, Oren, Richens, G. Reddy (lab site only), Kolossov, Tandon, Szegedy, Junfeng Fang, P. Henderson, Narasimhan, Sanjiv Kumar, Jimmy Ba, Bahdanau, Yihan Hu, Yanning Zhang, Aberman, Yi Wu (tracking), Navalpakkam, Bohan Yu, Mingqi Jiang, Li Fuxin, Yuchuan Tian, Jialin Zhu, He Wang (UCL), Kaihang Pan, Hanwang Zhang, Jonathan Long, Rabinovich, Liang Lu, Rofin, Madusanka, Batista-Navarro, Guan, Yuliang Liu (GitHub links to Scholar only), Pennington, Sivaprasad, Jingyang Yuan, Wangding Zeng. I did not search for Langkilde or Jungmee Lee (2013 UD paper last author), and the TACL ToT (Artzi/Zettlemoyer) is out of scope because it is a journal award.

How URLs were found: mostly from the person's own GitHub profile 'blog' field, or from search results that pointed to their page. Five came from aggregator pages (Piliouras, Avrithis, Kadkhodaie via search, Hashimoto, Jiaming Ji), and I confirmed each by page content. Tim Behrens's fmrib page and Rob Fergus's pmwiki page are older personal pages on university hosts. Scratch files are in <scratchpad>\aw (people.tsv, gh_out.tsv, final.tsv, entries_out.json).
